subject: Hosted API commit: EU region burst credits & marginal vs blended examples
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Wong <amy.wong@healthly.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API commit: EU region burst credits & marginal vs blended examples

Hi Amy,

Thanks for the productive conversation this morning. As discussed, attached is a concise commit proposal tailored for Healthly's EU-first rollout and the marketing-driven burst weeks you described. High level:

- 12 month committed spend (hosted per-token) covering both chat generation and embeddings (see attachment for token bands).
- Breakpoints at 0-2B, 2-7B, 7-20B tokens (monthly allocs aggregated for billing).
- Billing methodology option A: marginal per-token (you pay each band's rate for tokens in that band).
- Billing methodology option B: blended effective rate (single effective $/1K-token calculated over total).
- Temporary burst credits: 200M token buffer usable during campaign windows; unused bursts convert to a one-time credit at end of term.

I've called out two EU-specific items: 1) regional rate uplift of +4% to cover EU-hosted GPU capacity and data locality; 2) a clause to allow regional burst pools (so US traffic doesn't consume EU burst).

Two asks for you: (1) confirm whether the burst pool should be shared across products or isolated per environment; (2) confirm whether you prefer marginal billing or a blended effective-rate invoice for procurement simplicity.

Attachment: RWI-Proposal-Healthly-20280521.pdf (proposal + worked examples).

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

From: Amy Wong <amy.wong@healthly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-21T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit: EU region burst credits & marginal vs blended examples

Kimberly,

Thanks — proposal landed well with procurement. A couple of clarifying points from our side before we loop legal:

1) Burst behavior: we prefer a single shared burst pool across products (chat + embeddings) because campaigns may touch multiple endpoints. Can you confirm how usage attribution works when a burst is consumed?

2) Billing model: procurement likes the predictability of a blended effective rate on invoices (easier to reconcile), but finance is concerned that blended masks marginal economics for long-term forecasting. Is there a middle ground?

3) EU uplift: procurement accepts the +4% uplift if we can get a 30% cap on any single-month overage (i.e., if our monthly usage spikes >30% above committed monthly baseline, we get a one-month waiver before overage billing applies).

Also attaching a small sample of our May usage (healthly-may-usage-sample.csv) to help you run numbers.

Can Marcus or Dev provide worked examples (marginal vs blended) using our sample? With and without the shared burst pool would be ideal.

Best,
Amy Wong
Head of Platform, Healthly, Inc.
amy.wong@healthly.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Wong <amy.wong@healthly.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit: EU region burst credits & marginal vs blended examples

Amy — thanks for the clear asks. Quick technical and billing notes, plus two worked scenarios attached inline below. Dev, please add any infra caveats.

How shared burst attribution works (technical):
- Burst pool sits in the EU tenant and is drawn first for any request routed to EU-hosted endpoints.
- Attribution is by token counter per project/environment; when the pool is used, we decrement the burst balance and tag the token usage as "burst" in daily usage exports.
- If two endpoints concurrently draw the pool, tokens are allocated pro rata by app id for that minute.

Worked examples (using your sample file):
Scenario A — Marginal billing (no burst):
- Monthly tokens used: 3.1B
- Bands: 0-2B @ $0.0025/1K, 2-7B @ $0.0019/1K (EU uplift +4% applied)
- Charges: (2,000,000K * $0.0025) + (1,100,000K * $0.0019 * 1.04) = $5,000 + $2,173.6 = $7,173.60
- Effective rate = $7,173.60 / 3,100,000K = $0.002314/1K

Scenario B — Blended billing (no burst):
- Blended single rate offered for month based on negotiated price: $0.00225/1K (includes EU uplift already baked in).
- Charge: 3,100,000K * $0.00225 = $6,975.00
- Difference: blended looks cheaper on this month (-$198.60) but marginal protects Redwood on jump to higher bands.

Now include shared burst pool of 200M tokens consumed in that month (example):
Scenario A-1 — Marginal + Burst: same usage but 200M taken from burst pool (billed as 0 this month, reconciled at term-end if unused)
- Billable tokens by band reduce by 200M. Marginal math becomes: first 2B consumed, remaining billed in second band reduced accordingly. New charge ≈ $6,613.60 (roughly)
Scenario B-1 — Blended + Burst: blended rate * (3,100,000K - 200,000K) = 2,900,000K * $0.00225 = $6,525.00

Recommendation:
- For procurement simplicity, offer blended invoices month-to-month but include a line-item true-up report that shows marginal band consumption and the notional marginal bill. That gives finance a predictable invoice while keeping transparency.
- For the legal cap on overages: we can agree to the 30% one-month waiver for one instance per quarter. We prefer a true-up model at quarter-end for any sustained overage.

Dev — any operational limits for per-minute pro rata allocation?

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Wong <amy.wong@healthly.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-24T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit: EU region burst credits & marginal vs blended examples

Amy — looping back with an operationalized offer based on Marcus' worked examples and our standard contract terms. Key points summarized for procurement & legal: 

1) Billing behavior: Redwood will invoice monthly at a single blended effective rate (line-item: blended $/1K). Each monthly invoice is accompanied by a usage breakdown report (tokens by band, burst consumption, notional marginal amounts) so Healthly can reconcile internally.

2) Burst credits: 200M EU burst tokens are provided up-front and are consumed before invoiceable usage. Unused burst at term end converts to a one-time credit applied to the final invoice. Burst is shared across Healthly products in EU by default; we can split into per-environment pools if you prefer (note: split reduces flexibility).

3) Overages & caps: One-month waiver on single-month spikes up to 30% above committed monthly baseline (can be invoked once per quarter). Any sustained overage beyond the waiver is billed at marginal band rates. Quarterly true-ups reconcile to committed spend targets.

4) Regional uplift: +4% applied to base band prices to reflect EU hosting. For financial reporting, the blended rate we propose already includes this uplift.

Next steps: if this aligns, I'll route a near-final term sheet to DocuSign (link below) and pull legal in for a short redline pass. Please confirm acceptance of the shared burst pool and blended invoice preference by EOD Friday and I’ll circulate the DocuSign link.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/healthly-RWI-commit
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live for your EU launch.

Best,
